title: Expectations as Endowments: Evidence on Reference-Dependent Preferences from Exchange and Valuation Experiments

original_source.version_note: Complete original abstract only; full body inaccessible through attempted publisher/author routes.

central_claims: Expectations partly determine reference points: reduced trading probability increases retention, while higher acquisition probability raises willingness-to-accept by roughly 20–30%.

source_manifest.title: Expectations as Endowments: Evidence on Reference-Dependent Preferences from Exchange and Valuation Experiments
source_manifest.finding: Original central claims were recorded before follow-up grading.

source_manifest.title: Camerer et al. Evaluating replicability of laboratory experiments in economics — Supplement, Tables S1–S2
source_manifest.finding: The preregistered independent comparison tests whether high acquisition probability raises willingness-to-accept for a mug; replication N=262, original focal N=112, p=.055. The project only retested one selected result per paper.

source_manifest.title: Ericson and Fuster comment on replication
source_manifest.finding: Authors report preferred original regression specifications yield significant positive replication effects, whereas the project focal unadjusted comparison gives p=.055.

search_gaps: This is a complete but selected cohort of laboratory economics experiments, not a representative sample of research success.
The replication project tests only one selected comparison, not every claim or the entire theoretical contribution.
Outcome review prioritizes independently tested validation; absent adoption/utility evidence remains unknown.
Original assessment uses its complete abstract only; attempted full-text publisher/author routes were inaccessible. No fabricated full-text reading.
research.summary: Replication evidence depends on specification: the preregistered selected contrast narrowly misses p<.05, while original authors report significant replication in their preferred regressions. Neither blanket failure nor unqualified independent confirmation is justified from the sources inspected.
